text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Kenyan authorities launch full investigations to establish the source of a letter allegedly written by President Daniel arap Moi exonerating Kenyan-born Dubai-based businessman Ketan Somaia from dubious business dealings in Kenya.
- Kenyan runners clinch the overall team title in the World Cross Country Championships in Turin, for the 12th year.
- Police hold several people. among them staff members of the treasury, over an attempt to defraud the government of more than 150 million shillings ($2.7 million).

- The Supreme Council of Kenya Moslems vows to fight for a controversial plot in Nairobi city centre valued at 160 million shillings following President Moi's directive that hawkers be allowed to conduct business on the plot.
- The government launches investigations into an alleged lesbian sex scandal.
- A boy's body is found in the nose-wheel of a British Airways plane on arrival at London's Gatwick Airport.
- Police launch a massive man-hunt for about 500 minibus "matatu" operators turned-vigilante who on Friday lynched three suspected pick-pockets in the city.
- The management of Standard Chartered Bank launches an intensive security audit throughout its branches.
- Unscrupulous retail traders in the city and other urban centres in Kenya mint money from illegally hiked prices of milk.

- A number of officials and diplomats suggest Tanzanian President Benjamin Mkapa's refusal to attend the regional summit on eastern Zaire last week in Nairobi may have been due to concern over failure to invite Uganda.
- Kenya accepts a request from John Odongo, the self-styled dissident who claims to head a guerilla movement opposed to President Moi, to return home from exile in Ghana.
- Tanzania turns to the International Monetary Fund for assistance to review a proposed tax system that will be incorporated into the 1997/98 budget.
